The morning light spilled across rooftops, gentle, pale, and slow.
It touched the window frame with a whisper of blue.
Dust motes drifted upward, dancing in the narrow pale beams.
The clock on the wall softly marked a passing hour.
Outside, birds began their argument with bright and impatient wings.
A child laughed somewhere beyond the garden gate in morning.
Coffee slowly warmed my cupped hands, and the room exhaled.
I watched the steam rise, thin, soft, silver, and quiet.
The street below was busy with the passing morning footsteps.
Somewhere a door opened, letting out a small old song.
I remembered how rain sounded on the tin roof before.
It had a rhythm that was very patient and unending.
I wanted to keep the day, but days always refuse.
They quietly slip through fingers, leaving only pale shadows behind.
I opened the window and let the warm breeze in.
It carried scents of fresh grass, earth, and distant rain.
For a moment, the whole world seemed close and small.
Every object glowed, as if it had just been born.
I thought of the people I have loved and lost.
Their old voices returned, soft, steady, bright, and surprisingly alive.
I keep realizing that memory is never one fixed place.
It always changes with the light, the season, the mood.
Some mornings, grief feels very thin, like paper in wind.
Other mornings, it is a heavy, gray, silent, waiting companion.
I let it stay, then quietly opened the book again.
